messages:
maria: Heads up — CI SAST flagged a HIGH in ingest-api PR #4128 for possible log-injection in src/utils/serializer.go
scan-bot: [automated] SAST: HIGH - possible log injection - /ingest-api/src/utils/serializer.go:42 - https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/9876
ajay: can you paste the scanner output or snippet?
maria: here's what it flagged:
```
/ingest-api/src/utils/serializer.go:42:12: possible log injection: fmt.Sprintf(userInput)
 40 func Serialize(u User) string {
 41     // ...
>42     return fmt.Sprintf(u.LogFormat)
 43 }
```
lena: user-controlled format string. legit finding. quick remediation: fmt.Sprintf("%s", u.LogFormat) or better, structured logging (zap) to avoid format parsing.
devon: agreed. for premerge policy, any fmt.Sprintf with non-literal first arg -> FAIL. add to reviewer checklist.
maria: pushing a minimal fix now: replaced with log.Info("serialize", zap.String("format", u.LogFormat)). will re-run CI.
scan-bot: [automated] CI: rerun requested by maria - posting new scan to pr:4128
maria: CI reran, new SAST result shows PASS. PR is green but we need follow-ups: rule metadata, docs link, suppression guidance for fixtures.
ajay: I'll own CI gating changes. proposal: attach rule metadata fields (severity, docs_url, remediation_snippet) and set auto_create_ticket=false for noisy rules. add a small suppression whitelist limited to test fixtures.
oncall-eng: tagging @ajay — you're on security oncall today.
ajay: noted. also proposing SLA: initial triage for HIGH SAST = 4 business hours to assign.
devon: operational question — when we change logging calls, do we need RBAC changes for audit-writer SA? maria saw 403s in staging earlier.
lena: those 403s were from staging where the SA binding was missing. prod still has pubsub.publisher bound to audit-writer. I'll open infra ticket to add the staging binding and add a deploy preflight to verify audit-writer permissions.
ajay: follow RBAC change playbook: infra/iam PR, include audit evidence, request security review, and ensure the change is recorded in cloud audit logs (compliance requirement).
maria: noted. also, CI integration tests failing to decrypt a fixture with KMS key ci-fixtures-key — error: PermissionDenied.
devon: what's the approved pattern for CI KMS access? we shouldn't give keys to humans.
ajay: approved: use workload identity/ephemeral build tokens. grant cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypt to ci-runner service account scoped to the key resource. rotate keys 90 days. provide a dev-only key in dev project for local testing.
lena: will open infra ticket to add roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to projects/redwood-staging/serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com with a conditional binding on the key resource.
maria: quickfix pushed earlier unblocks PR. next steps should be documented so devs can fix quickly in future.
ajay: created ticket SDLC-3310: (1) add SAST rule metadata + remediation docs (go/python/node examples), (2) suppression whitelist for fixtures, (3) RBAC preflight for audit-writer across envs, (4) KMS CI access playbook + infra snippet. assigning to lena/devon - https://go.redwood/sec/SDLC-3310
maria: linked SDLC-3310 in PR and pinged @devon @lena
oncall-eng: handing off oncall — ajay -> devon for next 8h window
devon: will take over. plan: infra PRs for staging RBAC and KMS by tomorrow AM, docs changes by EOD. will post progress in this thread.
ajay: I'll update premerge bot to surface docs_url and remediation snippet inline in CI annotations.
lena: I'll draft remediation examples and a short reviewer playbook. maria — can you collect the common fmt patterns we see in other repos?
maria: yep, I can grep and send examples. thanks all :thumbsup:
scan-bot: [automated] ticket SDLC-3310 created by ajay
